name: Sins of the Tongue

counsel.text: This commandment binds the tongue to its good behaviour. God has set two natural fences to keep in the tongue, the teeth and lips; and this commandment is a third fence set about it, that it should not break forth into evil.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: Rise mightily against the first actings of thy distemper, its first conceptions; suffer it not to get the least ground. Do not say, "Thus far it shall go, and no farther." If it have allowance for one step, it will take another. It is impossible to fix bounds to sin. It is like water in a channel, -- if it once break out, it will have its course.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: The slanderer wounds three at once: he wounds him that is slandered; he wounds him to whom he reports the slander, by causing uncharitable thoughts to arise up in his mind against the party slandered; and he wounds his own soul, by reporting of another what is false.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: Love is a well-wisher, and it is rare to speak ill of him we wish well to. Love is that which cements Christians together; it is the healer of division, and the hinderer of slander.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: I say, then, by faith, be much in the consideration of that supply and the fulness of it that is in Jesus Christ, and how he can at any time give thee strength and deliverance.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: A man may wrong another as well by silence as by slander, when he knows him to be wrongfully accused, yet does not speak in his behalf. If others cast false aspersions on any, we should wipe them off.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I have sinned with my tongue. I spoke words that wounded, words that tore others down, and words that were unclean, and I spoke them about people made in your image. My words have shown what is in my heart, and I do not excuse them. I rest on Jesus Christ, my Advocate with you, whose blood was shed for these sins too. You have promised to forgive and cleanse all who confess, and I confess. Holy Spirit, make me hate this sin, give me courage to make it right with those I have wronged, and rule my mouth by your grace. Amen.

prayers.title: Before I speak
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, I am about to say something I should not. Stop my mouth. When you were mocked and struck, you did not answer back, and you are able to keep me quiet now. Holy Spirit, cool my anger and put love for this person in my heart, for Christ died for them as well. Let me say nothing at all, or say only what builds up and gives grace to the one who hears. Amen.

prayers.title: When I am drawn into gossip
prayers.text: Father, I am being drawn into talk about someone who is not here to answer. Give me the courage to be silent, to change the subject, or to speak up for them. Make me speak of others the way Christ speaks of me before you, with mercy and not with scorn. Take away my wish to be liked by sharing what I should keep. Fill my mouth with thanks instead of complaint. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When your words went wrong today, what was in your heart just before you spoke: anger, envy, pride, or the wish to be liked?
Whom did your words make smaller today, and what does that show about how you are seeing them, and how you are seeing God?
Did you say anything about someone today that you would not have said if they were in the room?
Is there anyone you need to go to and ask forgiveness for something you said, or a false report you need to set right?
When you complain about others, are you quietly complaining against God, who put them in your life?
Did your talk today give thanks and build others up, or was it mostly about yourself?
fleeActions: Close your mouth and step away from the conversation. Say nothing more until you have prayed.
If you are typing a message, delete it now. Do not send anything about this until tomorrow.
If others are gossiping, change the subject, or say plainly that you would rather not talk about someone who is not here.
Go to the person you spoke against, or the one you spoke to, and make it right today.
Pray for the person you were about to criticize by name, and thank God for one good thing in them.
Open your Bible to James 3 and read it slowly before you say another word.

afterFallReadings.text: Christ, by his intercession, calls for acquittance. Lord, he says, let the sinner be absolved from guilt; and in this sense he is called an advocate. 1 John 2:2. He requires that the sinner be set free in the court.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
